code.purpose: Editor content — the roomiest line-height in the system.

terminal.purpose: Terminal output — tighter line-height for scanning.

ui.purpose: Sidebar, status bar, title bar, panels, menus, notifications.

shadows.name: command-palette-float
shadows.purpose: The system's one floating overlay — the quick-input/command palette widget.

motion.name: tab-close-reveal
motion.purpose: Tab close button fades in on hover/active rather than sitting permanently visible.

motion.name: sash-hover-reveal
motion.purpose: Resize handles are invisible until hovered, then fade to a Signal Blue line.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Signal Blue action button — install, save, confirm.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #0078D4; color: #ffffff; padding: 4px 14px; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.07); border-radius: 2px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.1s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #026EC1; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #0078D4; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Neutral action button — cancel, secondary choice.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: #313131; color: #CCCCCC; padding: 4px 14px; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; border: none; border-radius: 2px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.1s ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #3C3C3C; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #0078D4; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Standard text input — settings, search, filters.
components.css: .ds-input { background: #313131; color: #CCCCCC; border: 1px solid #3C3C3C; border-radius: 4px; padding: 4px 8px; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #989898; } .ds-input:focus { outline: 1px solid #0078D4; outline-offset: -1px; border-color: transparent; }

components.name: Command Palette
components.description: The system's one floating, blurred surface — the quick-input overlay.
components.html:
Go to File...
Open Recent
components.css: .ds-palette { background: #222222; color: #CCCCCC; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08); border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: 0 12px 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.55); backdrop-filter: blur(20px); overflow: hidden; width: 320px; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; } .ds-palette-filter { width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; margin: 6px 8px; padding: 4px 8px; background: #313131; color: #CCCCCC; border: 1px solid #3C3C3C; border-radius: 6px; } .ds-palette-row { padding: 6px 12px; margin: 0 4px; border-radius: 4px; } .ds-palette-row.ds-active, .ds-palette-row:hover { background: rgba(0,120,212,0.2); }

components.name: Activity Bar Icon
components.description: Translucent glyph that brightens on hover/active, with a centered rounded-square highlight replacing VS Code's default edge indicator.
components.css: .ds-activity-bar { background: #181818; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; padding: 8px 0 0; width: 48px; } .ds-ab-icon { height: 36px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; position: relative; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.55); cursor: pointer; } .ds-ab-icon:hover, .ds-ab-icon.ds-checked { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.95); } .ds-ab-icon.ds-checked::after { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); width: 34px; height: 34px; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.10); border-radius: 6px; pointer-events: none; z-index: -1; }

components.name: Editor Tab
components.description: Compact 30px tab; active tab carries a Signal Blue top border, close button reveals on hover.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; background: #181818; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; } .ds-tab { height: 30px; line-height: 30px; padding: 0 10px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; color: #9D9D9D; border-right: 1px solid #2B2B2B; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tab.ds-active { background: #1F1F1F; color: #ffffff; border-top: 2px solid #0078D4; } .ds-tab-close { opacity: 0; transition: opacity 0.15s ease; } .ds-tab:hover .ds-tab-close, .ds-tab.ds-active .ds-tab-close { opacity: 1; }

narrative.overview:
Null IDE is a VS Code fork with the ornament sanded off, not a new visual language bolted on. The chrome sits in near-black grays (#181818 down to #000000 on the OLED variant) with a single accent — Signal Blue (#0078D4), stock VS Code blue kept deliberately rather than replaced — used only where the UI needs to say "this is active, this is focused, this is progress." The mark itself, the ∅ symbol, is monochrome: white stroke on a near-black gradient badge, no color at all. Emptiness is the aesthetic, not an absence of polish.

This is a personal daily-driver, not a marketing surface — PRODUCT.md is explicit that the only user who matters is the developer running it. That shows up as restraint everywhere: no gradients, no decorative color, no shadow except where a floating surface genuinely needs to separate itself from the canvas beneath it. The workbench stays close to upstream VS Code conventions on purpose — familiar control shapes, default paddings, standard iconography — with edits concentrated on density (30px tabs, 36px activity-bar rows, a 6px scrollbar) and on removing default chrome that competed with the content (the activity bar's left-edge active-indicator is explicitly hidden in favor of a centered highlight square).

Earlier project notes described a teal/indigo brand palette. That palette does not exist anywhere in the shipped theme, icon set, or workbench CSS — the real, implemented accent is VS Code blue, and the app icon is achromatic. This file documents what is actually built.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black, borderless-feeling chrome with 1px dividers, never a filled panel-on-panel look
One accent color, used sparingly for state (focus, active, progress, links) — never decoratively
Monospace everywhere code or terminal output appears; system UI font everywhere else — the two never mix
Flat by default; the command palette is the system's one deliberate floating, blurred surface
A separate, wide semantic color set (9 hues) exists only inside the file/folder icon theme — it never bleeds into the UI accent

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue is the only color allowed to mean "interactive" or "active." Success/warning/error are reserved for git and diagnostic state and must never be reused as a UI accent, and no second brand color (teal, indigo, or otherwise) gets introduced — the accent stays singular.

rules.name: The Two-Font Rule
rules.body: Exactly two font roles exist: monospace for code/terminal, system UI font for chrome. Nothing else — no serif, no display weight, no third face — is introduced anywhere in the workbench.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest, separated only by 1px Divider borders. The command palette is the system's single deliberate exception, justified because it's an ephemeral overlay, not a docked panel — no other surface should adopt its shadow/blur treatment.

dos: Do treat Signal Blue (#0078D4) as the only UI accent — focus, active, progress, links, primary actions.
Do keep code/terminal on the monospace stack and chrome on the system UI font; never let one bleed into the other's surfaces.
Do keep new surfaces flat with a 1px Divider border; reserve shadow + blur for genuinely transient floating overlays, matching the command palette's justification.
Do color folder/file icons only from the established 9-hue semantic set on the slate-gray base — don't invent a new hue for a new folder pattern.
donts: Don't introduce teal or indigo (or any second brand color) as a UI accent — despite older project notes, nothing in the shipped theme, icon set, or workbench CSS uses them; the mark itself is monochrome.
Don't restore VS Code's default left-edge activity-bar active-indicator — it's deliberately replaced by the centered rounded-square highlight.
Don't add drop shadows to docked, permanent panels (sidebar, bottom panel, status bar) — shadow is reserved for the command palette's transient-overlay case.
